title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 26-29): L is a lattice of subsets of a space, such as polyhedral or semi-algebraic sets in Grothendieck's 'tame topology'. A 'figure' F is a set of closed pieces A ⊂ L whose 'interiors' A° partition the support |F| = ∪A, so it behaves like a finite cell decomposition or stratification. Three order relations are used. F' ≤ F means F' is a closed subfigure of F. F' ≼ F is a subdivision/refinement relation. F' ≪ F is a weaker relation combining the two, roughly 'F' refines part of F'.

On p.27 Grothendieck defines the intersection figure: F.G = {A∩B : A∈F, B∈G, A°∩B°≠∅}. The cells (A∩B)° = A°∩B° partition |F|∩|G|; they are the classes of the join of the two equivalence relations induced on |F|∩|G|. The inline diagram re-expresses this with surjections S→I, S'→I' onto ordered index sets, giving A_{(i,i')} = A_i ∩ A'_{i'}.

Page 28 states the following.
(1) Proposition: F.G is an infimum of F and G for ≪. It is called the 'figure intersection'.
(2) Warning: do not confuse F.G with F∩G, the set of pieces common to F and G, viewed as subsets of P(L). F∩G will only be used when F and G are compatible (they agree on the overlap of their supports), and then the two coincide. So F.G is the right notion of intersection.
(3) The construction works for an arbitrary family (F_i), with |∧F_i| = ∩|F_i|.
(4) The existence of infima for ≪ is compared to a 'directedness' property (reading uncertain). In modern terms: the poset of figures under refinement is cofiltered, so subdivisions form a directed system.
(5) Property: if F' ≪ (or ≼) F, then F'.G ≼ F.G. This is immediate on supports: the intersection is unchanged in support and only refined.

Page 29 continues with monotonicity of F.G in each of ≪, ≼ and ≤. That yields an axiom C6 of an abstract axiom system, after which C7 (extension of a subdivision of a closed subfigure to the whole figure) is attacked.

Purpose: build an axiomatic 'algebra of figures', i.e. a combinatorial framework for tame/stratified spaces and their subdivisions. This is presumably aimed at the dévissage programme for tame topology sketched in the Esquisse.
errors: For an infinite family, |∧F_i| = ∩|F_i| requires the infinite intersections of pieces to lie in L and the resulting cell set to be a figure (e.g. finite). In a general lattice of tame sets this fails: an infinite intersection of definable sets need not be definable. So 'famille quelconque' needs a finiteness or completeness hypothesis on L, or should read 'finite family'.

F.G is a meet for ≪ but not a common refinement in the ≼ sense, since its support shrinks to |F|∩|G|. The page is careful about this, but the exact definitions of ≪ and ≼ come from earlier pages, so the claim cannot be fully checked here.

ideas.what: Intersection figure F.G = {A∩B : A°∩B°≠∅}, the common refinement of two cell decompositions restricted to the intersection of their supports
ideas.modern_name: common refinement / meet of stratifications or partitions; product cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL topology and o-minimal cell decomposition theory (van den Dries et al.)

ideas.what: Distinguishing F.G from the naive set-theoretic F∩G, the two coinciding exactly for compatible figures
Existence of infima for the refinement relation, viewed as a directedness (cofiltered) property of the poset of figures
ideas.modern_name: cofiltered poset of subdivisions (as used to define invariants by limits over subdivisions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL topology and Čech-type constructions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures in general terms, without this formalism

ideas.what: Monotonicity of F.G under refinement (and, on the next page, under closed subfigures), feeding abstract axioms C6/C7
ideas.modern_name: axiomatics of subdivision; extension of subdivisions from subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology (e.g. Zeeman, Rourke–Sanderson) for the concrete statements

missed.claim: This page is part of an unpublished axiomatic 'algebra of figures' (axioms C1–C7…): an abstract order-theoretic framework for stratified/tame cell decompositions with three interacting relations (≪, ≼, ≤). The page content itself is routine. But the overall attempt to axiomatize subdivision theory, independently of o-minimality, seems not to have been taken up in the literature.
missed.quote: Cette propriété d'existence d'un Inf pour la relation ≪ s'apparente à une propriété de "une direction"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a record of how Grothendieck intended to found 'tame topology' combinatorially in 1986. That is relevant to historians, and possibly to people axiomatizing stratified spaces (exit-path categories, o-minimal structures).

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine common-refinement construction and its basic order properties. Interest is mainly historical: it documents the unpublished 1986 axiomatic programme for figures and tame topology, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'i.e. on l'appelle la "figure intersection" F.G' rather than 'l'ensemble [?] C'.
'Donc [?] la bonne notion d'intersection est L [?] F.G' — probably 'est la F.G' (or 'le F.G').
's'apparente [?]' is plausibly 'l'apparente'. The word read as 'une direction' is very uncertain; it may refer to filtrant/directed-ness.
In the final Propriété, the hypothesis may be 'F' ≼ F' rather than 'F' ≪ F' (the symbol is partly overwritten). The diagonal strokes through 'F'.G' and 'F.G' are pen marks, not part of the notation.

Last lines: '(immédiat sur les supports) : seule la division change / support inchangé par un raffinement' is a plausible reading of the garbled '(immédiat sur son support) : S la division … inchangée par un raffinement'.
